quizName: DMV Practice Test #7 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Where is the horn button usually located?
questions.correctAnswerText: By the left handgrip
questions.explanation: Learn where all your motorcycle controls are before you start riding. The horn button is usually located next to the left handgrip.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Signal, use your mirrors, and turn your head.
Turn your head and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, use your mirrors, and turn your head.
questions.explanation: Always signal before you change lanes. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to see if other vehicles are nearby before changing lanes.

questions.question: A driver making eye contact with you:

options.text: Does not mean that they will properly yield to you.
Guarantees that they will properly yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not mean that they will properly yield to you.
questions.explanation: Do not rely on eye contact to know a driver will yield to you. Drivers often look directly at motorcyclists but do not actually see them.

questions.question: When following another vehicle as a beginning rider, you should:

options.text: Maintain a minimum four-second following distance.
Get as close to the other vehicle as possible.
Never be concerned about your following distance.
Always ride in the left portion of the lane so the driver can easily see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Maintain a minimum four-second following distance.
questions.explanation: Beginning riders should keep at least four seconds of distance between themselves and the vehicle ahead. Increase this distance if conditions are poor.

questions.question: Where is the greatest potential for conflict between motorcycle operators and other drivers?
questions.correctAnswerText: At intersections
questions.explanation: Intersections are where most conflicts between motorcyclists and other drivers happen. Be extra careful when approaching and going through intersections.

questions.question: When being passed, all of the following are potential hazards, except:

options.text: Objects being thrown from other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Headlights.
questions.explanation: When being passed, watch out for the passing vehicle's mirrors hitting you. Be aware of wind gusts from the passing vehicle and objects that passengers might throw.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: A motorcycle with a sidecar:

options.text: Can tip over if making a turn too fast.
Is designed to take corners at any speed.
Should not be used for loading items.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can tip over if making a turn too fast.
questions.explanation: Even with three wheels on the ground, a sidecar can tip over if you turn too sharply or go too fast around a corner.

questions.question: In a normal turn:

options.text: The motorcycle and rider should lean together.
The motorcycle and rider should lean in opposite directions.
The motorcycle should lean, but the rider should not.
The rider should lean, but the motorcycle should not.

questions.correctAnswerText: The motorcycle and rider should lean together.
questions.explanation: In normal turns, the motorcycle and rider lean at the same angle. In slow, tight turns, only the motorcycle leans while the rider stays upright.

questions.question: Crashes are more likely to occur among:

options.text: Those who have completed a safety course.

questions.correctAnswerText: Beginning riders.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen most often to new riders who are untrained and do not know their motorcycle well.

questions.question: If you are carrying a passenger, they should:

options.text: Lean with you as you lean.
Sit as far back on the seat as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean with you as you lean.
questions.explanation: Passengers should lean when you lean. A passenger should sit as far forward as possible without getting in your way. They should hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: To reduce the chance of a crash, you should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Be ready to react to hazards.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hope another driver sees you.
questions.explanation: To lower your crash risk, make sure other drivers can see you. Tell them what you plan to do by using turn signals and good lane position. Keep space around you. Look ahead and watch for hazards so you can react quickly.

questions.question: You should choose your lane position to:

options.text: Reduce your space around you and make sure others can see you.
Increase your space around you and make sure others can see you.
Increase your chances of hitting road hazards and let others pass easily.
Reduce your chances of hitting road hazards and stay close behind other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your space around you and make sure others can see you.
questions.explanation: A good lane position gives you more space, lets others see you, keeps you away from wind from other vehicles, and avoids blind spots. It stops other drivers from sharing your lane and gives you a way to escape if something goes wrong. Choose a position that gives you the most space around you.

questions.question: An experienced rider:

options.text: Changes position within their lane as road and traffic conditions change.
Stays in one part of the lane at all times.
Moves side to side within the lane to be more visible.
Rides only on the oily part of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Changes position within their lane as road and traffic conditions change.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle riders have three lane positions to choose from within their lane. Pick the safest position based on the road and traffic around you.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Left turn
questions.explanation: Riders can use hand signals along with or instead of turn signals. When your left arm is straight out to the side, it means you plan to turn left or change lanes to the left.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, you should:

options.text: Speed up to get out of the wobble.
Hold the handlebars tight and slowly close the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handlebars tight and slowly close the throttle.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up during a wobble. It will make things worse. Instead, grip the handlebars firmly, slowly reduce your speed by closing the throttle, and lean forward and down. Pull off the road as soon as you safely can.

questions.question: To see better when preparing to pass a vehicle on its left, you should:

options.text: Ride in the left part of your lane.
Ride in the right part of your lane.
Ride in the middle of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the left part of your lane.
questions.explanation: When preparing to pass on the left, ride in the left part of your lane. This helps you see ahead better and makes oncoming traffic more likely to see you.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Signs that show road rules, like speed limits, are usually rectangular with white background and black letters or symbols. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: Riding next to another rider:

options.text: Lets you use more of the road.
Should be avoided because it limits your ways to escape danger.
Lets you talk to each other easily.
Makes it easier for other drivers to pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be avoided because it limits your ways to escape danger.
questions.explanation: Do not ride next to another motorcycle. It limits both riders' escape routes if a hazard appears.

questions.question: The gear shift lever is located:

options.text: In front of the left footrest.
In front of the right footrest.

questions.correctAnswerText: In front of the left footrest.
questions.explanation: The gear shift lever is in front of the left footrest. You operate it with your left foot. Lift the lever to shift to a higher gear. Press it down to shift to a lower gear.

questions.question: Many factors affect blood alcohol concentration (BAC). Which one does NOT affect BAC?
questions.correctAnswerText: Height
questions.explanation: BAC depends on how much alcohol you drink, how fast you drink it, and your body weight. Height does not affect BAC.

questions.question: Bright-colored helmets:

options.text: Make it easier for others to see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make it easier for others to see you.
questions.explanation: Bright-colored helmets are recommended. They protect you in a crash and help other drivers see you on the road.

questions.question: Keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles helps because:

options.text: You can pass dangers more quickly.
Your view is narrower so you stay focused.
You have more time to react to what other drivers do.
You can follow the next vehicle's path more easily.

questions.correctAnswerText: You have more time to react to what other drivers do.
questions.explanation: Keeping space between you and other vehicles gives you a better view of hazards, more time to react, and more room to maneuver.

questions.question: For normal braking:

options.text: Alternate between front and rear brakes to make them last longer.
Use both the front and rear brakes together.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes together.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes together every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: After you enter a turn, roll on the throttle and:

options.text: Keep a steady speed or speed up slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a steady speed or speed up slowly.
questions.explanation: Roll on the throttle through a turn to keep your suspension stable. Maintain a steady speed or accelerate gradually through the turn.
